previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease s/p CABG and stents, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for sudden-onset substernal chest pain and ST elevations on EKG, concerning for STEMI. Cardiac catheterization revealed no new obstructive lesions, suggesting an aborted myocardial infarction. She was managed medically with dual antiplatelet therapy and adjustment of beta-blocker for hypertension. During admission, her elevated creatinine (1.4–1.5 mg/dL) was attributed to acute tubular necrosis, likely from recent dehydration. Her poorly controlled diabetes (A1c 12.5%) prompted an increase in Lantus insulin from 50 to 65 units daily, with transition to an insulin pen for ease of use. An infected epidermal cyst on her back was incised and drained, with culture growing Staphylococcus aureus, treated with doxycycline. Prurigo nodules from chronic scratching were managed with triamcinolone cream. Social work addressed her non-adherence and lack of support, recommending evaluation for long-term assisted care. She was discharged home with services and follow-up arranged.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric CT imaging was performed through the chest after the
administration of 100 mL Omnipaque nonionic intravenous contrast according to
CTA protocol.  Post processing performed in the coronal and sagittal planes.

COMPARISON:  Prior CTA from ___.

FINDINGS:

There are atherosclerotic changes of the thoracic aorta and coronary vessels. 
There is no evidence to suggest aortic dissection.  No pulmonary emboli are
identified.  The patient is status post median sternotomy for a previous CABG.
The heart size is enlarged.  There is no pericardial effusion.  There is no
significant mediastinal, hilar, or axillary lymphadenopathy.  The lungs and

visualized portions of the thyroid are normal.  The visualized upper abdominal
structures are normal.  A peritoneal catheter is partially visualized in the
left upper quadrant.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.
